newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise on international demand.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise on international demand.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose for the fourth consecutive day on Monday, driven higher by extensive foreign activity and traders predicted the uptrend was likely to continue all week.
"Obviously foreigners are buying a lot and I hope this will keep pushing the prices up," said Natasa Kovacic, a trader at brokerage Centralna.
The SBI index rose 1.35 percent or 19.51 points to 1,459.66. Over four days the index has climbed 4.51 percent.

Traders said an expected parliamentary "yes" vote to bring local legislation into line with EU regulations could push the index even higher but cautioned failure to approve the legilsation would have a negative effect on share prices.

Parliament is expected to change the constitution later on Monday in order to enable foreigners to own land. The move is a precondition for ratification of an EU association agreement signed last year.
Overall 12 shares rose, two fell and three were flat, while 11 were untraded. Turnover rose to 273.1 million tolars from 255.0 million.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 9.94 percent to 5,970 tolars on low volume of just 19 shares.
Food maker Kolinska was the most active share, rising 3.46 percent to 2,300 tolars on volume of 9,160 shares.
"Kolinska, Lek and Petrol are and will remain among the most attractive shares for foreign investors," one broker said.
Drug maker Lek had the highest turnover, rising 1.49 percent or 500 tolars to 34,000 tolars on volume of 3,977 shares for total turnover of 135.1 million tolars.
Some traders forecasted Lek could rise as high as 40,000 tolars over the summer.
Petrol trader Petrol, rose 1.15 percent to 21,170 tolars on volume of 3,591 shares.
Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska Banka led the decliners, easing 0.67 percent to 13,400 tolars on volume of 45 shares.
